newsitem.title: USA: SEC settles with trader who lost for Common Fund.
newsitem.headline: SEC settles with trader who lost for Common Fund.

text.p: Former derivatives trader Kent Ahrens, who lost $137.6 million for the Common Fund through unauthorized trading, was permanently barred from working as a securities broker or investment adviser, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Tuesday.

The trades occurred between 1992 and 1995 in an account that Ahrens's former firm, First Capital Strategists, managed on behalf of the $18 billion Common Fund, which manages money for more than 1,400 U.S. colleges and universities.
Ahrens also agreed to pay back $182,000 of commissions he earned on the unauthorized trades.
The SEC said Ahrens entered a consent agreement settling fraud charges stemming from the losses without admitting or denying the allegations.

Ahrens was supposed to manage the Common Fund's account using a low-risk strategy known as equity index arbitrage in which options or futures contracts are bought or sold and hedged with an offsetting position in stocks, the SEC said.

But sometime in 1992, Ahrens incurred a loss in the Common Fund account and in an attempt to recoup the loss began to use riskier investment strategies, the SEC alleged. Ahrens did not inform the Common Fund or First Capital of the loss, SEC said.
For three years, Ahrens bet without hedging that the stock market would decline, SEC said. As the market continued rising, losses in the Common Fund account mounted.

Ahrens earned $455,465 in commissions on the trades, but the SEC said the former trader has only enough money left to repay a portion of the sum. For the same reason, the SEC said it was waiving possible civil penalties.
The SEC said its investigation is continuing.
In related actions, a U.S. Attorney in Pennsylvania charged Ahrens with one count of wire fraud and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission also filed an action.
